newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: North Korea nuclear pact back on track--Seoul.
newsitem.headline: North Korea nuclear pact back on track--Seoul.

text.p: A landmark nuclear agreement with North Korea will be back on track next week when a consortium signs protocols with Pyongyang to build light-water reactors, Seoul officials said on Friday.

It is the first concrete step to repair the political damage from the incursion of a North Korean submarine into the South in September. The move follows an apology by Pyongyang over the incident on Sunday.

South Korea's Deputy Prime Minister Kwon O-kie told government and ruling party officials that two protocols would be signed by the Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organisation (KEDO) and North Korea.
"This incident taught North Korea that provocation has always had its price," Kwon was quoted as saying by his spokesman.

The incursion froze all contacts between the two Koreas. South Korea is largely financing the reactors promised to North Korea in a 1994 agreement with the United States that halted Pyongyang's suspected nuclear weapons programme.
The protocols cover the selection of the site for the reactors and specify services to be provided by North Korea for the project, a KEDO official said.
